type_guard_matching_rules.status: independently derived by the reviewer from the source BEFORE comparing with the catalogue, and verified word for word
type_guard_matching_rules.p3: A TYPE IS type guard statement matches the selector if the dynamic type and kind type parameter values of the selector are the same as those specified by the statement. A CLASS IS type guard statement matches if the dynamic type of the selector is an extension of the type specified.
type_guard_matching_rules.p4_selection_order: If a TYPE IS guard matches, that block is selected. Otherwise, if exactly one CLASS IS guard matches, that block is selected. Otherwise, if several CLASS IS guards match, the one selected specifies A TYPE THAT IS AN EXTENSION OF ALL THE TYPES SPECIFIED IN THE OTHERS. Otherwise, if a CLASS DEFAULT guard appears, that block is selected. Otherwise, no block is selected.
type_guard_matching_rules.verdict: the catalogue states the most-specific-match rule correctly - this is the single easiest thing in Clause 11 to paraphrase almost-correctly, and everything downstream depends on it

attribution_table_audit.c1168_reading: CONFIRMED CORRECT. C1168 does NOT prohibit one TYPE IS guard together with one CLASS IS guard specifying the same type; it prohibits the same type being specified in more than one TYPE IS, and in more than one CLASS IS, separately.
attribution_table_audit.c1172_reading: CONFIRMED CORRECT. C1172 is NOT a blanket ban on a textual EXIT appearing inside a DO CONCURRENT construct; it turns on which construct the EXIT statement BELONGS TO. The negatives isolate exactly that property.

oracle_discipline.no_duplicating_intrinsic: No plan uses SAME_TYPE_AS or EXTENDS_TYPE_OF as an oracle basis; doing so would duplicate the feature under test.
oracle_discipline.observability_scoping: Which block executed is observable; which guard was evaluated is not, and Fortran guarantees no short-circuiting. The unobservability claim is scoped so it does not suppress the observable block-selection fact - an overbroad claim would itself be a defect.
oracle_discipline.non_vacuity: Declared and dynamic types are made genuinely to differ so a wrong selection rule is caught, and sentinels are distinct from every value any block could write.
